title: Annotatio IV §.XV open: Eleventh century — Hildebrandine age; papal tyranny at its summit
pass_a_gloss: §. XV. The ELEVENTH AGE is commonly called Hildebrandine, because by the malice and tyranny of Pope Hildebrand, or Gregory VII, it is most infamous of all, when Anti-Christianism — i.e. Papal Dominion and Tyranny — just as in the VIIth Age in Boniface III, constituted Oecumenical Bishop by the Parricide Phocas, it obtained its full birth, so through Hildebrandine arts and this man’s most insolent Dictates it was led to its summit.
pass_b_english: §.XV: the ELEVENTH age is commonly called Hildebrandine — most infamous by Pope Hildebrand (Gregory VII)’s malice and tyranny.
Papal dominion, born full under Boniface III (Phocas, Age VII), was driven to its summit by Hildebrandine arts and his insolent Dictates.
source_text: §. XV. UNDECIMUM SECULUM Hildebrandinum vulgò dicitur, quod malitia & tyrannide Hildebrandi Papæ, seu Gregorii VII, omnium maximè infame est, cum Anti-Christianismus, i. e. Dominatus Tyrannisque Papalis, uti Seculo VII. in Bonifacio III, à Parricida Phoca, Episcopo Oecumenico constituto, plenam suam genituram consecutus, ita per artes Hildebrandinas Dictatusque hujus hominis insolentissimos, ad fastigium perductus est.
